title: External validation of the Epic Sepsis Model
system_purpose: Predict sepsis onset in hospitalized patients and raise a clinician alert
decision_impact: The alert changes how soon clinicians look for sepsis and how fast antibiotics are started
verified_facts: A retrospective cohort of 27697 patients with 38455 hospitalizations at Michigan Medicine found the model had a hospitalization-level area under the curve of 0.63 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.62 to 0.64, which the authors describe as poor discrimination and calibration.
reported_harm: Missed deterioration and alert fatigue, both of which can delay treatment of a time-critical condition
quantitative_evidence: Sepsis occurred in 2552 of 38455 hospitalizations (7 percent). The model failed to identify 1709 sepsis patients (67 percent) while alerting on 6971 hospitalizations (18 percent), and it added only 183 of those 2552 sepsis patients (7 percent) who had not already received timely antibiotics.
limitations: Retrospective, single academic health system in the United States; the study evaluates one vendor configuration and does not measure what local tuning at other hospitals would have produced.

title: Racial bias in a commercial population health risk algorithm
system_purpose: Rank patients by predicted need so the sickest are enrolled in extra care management
decision_impact: The score decided which patients were referred into a high-risk care management program
affected_groups: Black patients;patients with chronic illness;care managers
verified_facts: The study found that at a given risk score Black patients were considerably sicker than White patients, and traced the cause to the algorithm predicting future health care cost rather than illness, because less money is historically spent on care for Black patients.
reported_harm: Unequal access to extra care, a discrimination harm produced by a proxy choice rather than by a protected attribute
quantitative_evidence: Removing the cost proxy would raise the share of Black patients receiving additional help from 17.7 percent to 46.5 percent, in an algorithm the authors describe as affecting millions of patients.
limitations: One commercial algorithm at one United States academic hospital, without an independent technical audit; the protected groups and access patterns differ from the Vietnamese setting, so the mechanism transfers but the numbers do not.
